newsitem.title: USA: Stocks extend rally on bullish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Stocks extend rally on bullish sentiment.

text.p: Stocks rose on Friday, basking in another day of investor bullishness about the U.S. economy and adding more power to Wall Street's recent breakneck rally.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 39.36 points or 0.51 percent at 7,816.42, extending Thursday's gains.
In the broader market, however, declining issues outpaced advances by a 7-5 margin on volume of 419 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index rose 4.31 points to 1,451.45.
"The market is in great shape and fundamentals are strong," said Bill Allyn, head of trading at Jeffries & Co. "I wish it were more complicated than that, but it's not."
Share prices rose amid general optimism about the U.S. economy, which is showing signs of moderate growth and tame inflation, analysts said.
They said there is a growing consensus that the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates at its July meeting, and long bond yields are coming down.
"The stock market is also getting great support from the bond market here," said Tom Carpenter, a managing director and chief economist of at ASB Capital Management Inc.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose 9/32, reducing its yield to 6.66 percent from 6.68 percent at Thursday's close.
"As long as bonds keep rising, it keeps sellers out of the market," said Dan Ascani, president and director of research at Global Market Strategists Inc.

But he said the stock market was showing signs of a short-term peak which would prelude a consolidation. "We are seeing a lot of industry rotation. "The general message has been to reject the techs and to stick to the cyclicals and the bank and financial stocks."
Traders were waiting to see if the tobacco industry and state attorneys general would announce a settlement later in the day.
Philip Morris Cos Inc. led the list of most active stocks on the New York Stock Exchange, trading down 3/8 at 47. RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. was off 1/2 at 35-3/8.

The tobacco talks have been going on since April. They are aimed at a broad settlement of the huge legal claims against the industry in return for increased regulation, advertising curbs and health care programmes.
A news conference regarding the negotiations was tentatively scheduled for 1:30 p.m. EDT.

Among other active issues, shares of Ikon Office Solutions Inc. tumbled after the company warned that its earnings for the third and fourth quarters would not meet analysts' expectations. Ikon sank 8-3/8 to 23-5/8.
